review.notes: The lineage has only one transition and it is cosmetic, so it is not recorded as a change: v0 (FET-EN012, 2005-03-01, the GOAT entry's exact text) -> v1 (DR3-EN132, 2006-11-25, the pinned cdb text) drops 'As long as this card remains face-up on the field' and modernises 'increase the ATK of this card by 500 points' to 'this card gains 500 ATK'. Both scripts already require the Panda to be face-up and related to the effect at target and resolution (atktg/atkop), so the dropped clause changes nothing. The remaining script difference (RESET_EVENT|RESETS_STANDARD vs RESET_EVENT+RESETS_STANDARD) is the same value. Nothing in the packet or the shared briefs dates the battle-destruction timing ruling, so effective is left empty.

event.historical_text: As long as this card remains face-up on the field, each time a Beast-Type monster(s) on the field is destroyed, increase the ATK of this card by 500 points.
event.summary: Period trigger timing, not a text erratum. The modern script has a single mandatory EVENT_DESTROYED field trigger whose filter inspects the destroyed monster's previous state (IsPreviousLocation(LOCATION_MZONE), IsPreviousPosition(POS_FACEUP), GetPreviousRaceOnField). The GOAT variant removes battle destruction from that trigger (adding 'not c:IsReason(REASON_BATTLE)' to the filter) and registers a clone on EVENT_BATTLED whose condition tests the attacker or attack target while it is still on the field: 'c:IsLocation(LOCATION_MZONE) and c:IsPosition(POS_FACEUP) and c:IsRace(RACE_BEAST) and c:IsBattleDestroyed()'. So in the era a Beast destroyed by battle registers the +500 ATK from its live on-field state during the battle, before the destruction is applied, instead of from its previous state afterwards. Upstream's note: 'Battle destroyed registers while the mosnter is on field.'
